candidates: Always use `??` (nullish coalescing) instead of `||` (logical OR) when supplying default fallbacks for config values. `||` treats `0` and `false` as falsy and silently overrides intentional zero/false values, while `??` only falls back on `null` or `undefined`.

Avoid calling `getConfig()` multiple times within a single function, and never call it inside recursive or shared helper functions where it would be re-invoked on every recursion. Instead, call `getConfig()` once at the top-level entry point and pass the resulting config object as an explicit parameter down to helpers and recursive calls. This prevents redundant work and avoids stale-config bugs when multiple diagrams are rendered in the same session.

Use ES6 template literals (backtick strings with `${}` interpolation) for all dynamic string construction — especially for SVG attribute values like `transform` — rather than concatenating strings with `+`.

Place test files co-located with the module under test (e.g., `src/utils/subGraphTitleMargins.spec.ts` next to `src/utils/subGraphTitleMargins.ts`) rather than adding new tests to the shared `utils.spec.ts`, which is intentionally being split up. Also name utility files after the module's domain/concern (e.g., `subGraphTitleMargins.ts`) rather than after a specific exported function (e.g., `getSubGraphTitleMargins.ts`).
